reviewer.method: Fresh independent pass on the newly rebuilt 60s sample (output/preview.mp4, sha256 4604bca9118ab6e48756af9e344e3a2b0724290c72b2649fab098e253d23d661, re-verified by direct sha256sum against evidence.json's output_sha256 -- exact match, so no re-encode drift is possible). Read output/preview-reference/evidence.json and review-template.json for the shot list and exact frame_index/source_time of every start/mid/end artifact, then opened all 42 provided phase PNGs (shots 0-13) directly. For the four elements the brief named as new or reworded, extracted additional frames myself with ffmpeg rather than relying on the provided PNGs alone: shot-0's metronome at 0.1/0.5/0.9/1.3/1.7/2.1/2.5/2.8s (8 frames, cropped and tiled to confirm the pendulum swings rather than sits frozen, and to re-measure its clearance from the sliding article sheet at every sample); shot-5's new label at its start/mid/end PNGs plus two lanczos-upscaled crops of the x140-620,y80-190 region to inspect the laptop bezel/label interaction pixel-by-pixel; shot-9's reworked captions at start/mid/end; and shot-13's reworked claim card and new question at 12 additional ffmpeg frames (56.1 through 58.8s in ~0.2-0.3s steps), cropped to the question/underline region and vstacked into one tile to confirm the underline is a normal progressive left-to-right stroke rather than a stray dot artifact. Cross-checked all four edits against project.json's actual layer coordinates (grep + direct reads around the shot-0, shot-5, shot-9 and shot-13 timeline blocks) to get exact x/y/size figures rather than estimating from pixels alone, and against tools/script.mjs to confirm the new spoken line and the unchanged scene-3 narration line both match what is rendered (noting that narasi.md, the project's own human-readable doc, is stale and still shows the pre-revision scene-1 line -- a documentation hygiene issue, not a render defect). Read review/findings-preview-v6.json in full (both halves, 2162 lines) as the last passing baseline (14/14 shots) and used its per-shot, per-check text as the comparison basis for every shot in this pass, re-confirming by direct frame inspection (not just reading v6's prose) for shots 1-4, 6-8 and 10-12, which the brief described as untouched by this revision. Located and re-verified the b1-ryan-v4 reference file by sha256 (111c241a836a0c26b27df2cbff3ba5697b97460dbb873b68dd2f6eda2383b3fc, matches evidence.json) and re-ran ffmpeg ebur128 on both the full sample and the reference to re-measure loudness independently rather than trust the figures already on file (sample: I=-20.3 LUFS, true peak -2.0 dBFS, LRA 17.6 LU; reference: I=-20.5 LUFS, true peak -1.6 dBFS, LRA 2.9 LU -- both within rounding of the prior pass's figures). Sound was measured with ffmpeg only; it was not listened to by ear.
